body.en: *Outsourcing* means contracting out some of a firm's non-core activities (and sometimes core ones) to outside agencies that specialise in them. Firms outsource to focus on their core competence, to get specialised skills, to cut costs (through economies of scale of the service provider and cheaper labour elsewhere), to speed up work and to grow faster without adding staff. Commonly outsourced: customer support, accounting and payroll, IT services, logistics, cleaning and security, and research.

body.en: *Merits*: focus on core work, access to expertise, cost savings, faster growth and stimulation of employment in the provider's country. Concerns: confidentiality of data may be at risk, the firm loses some control, customer service quality may suffer, there may be ethical issues (low wages, job losses at home), and dependence on the provider is risky. Firms reduce these risks with careful selection of providers, clear contracts and service-level agreements.

problem.en: Why is India a popular outsourcing destination? Give four reasons.

steps.en: A large pool of educated, English-speaking workers.
Lower labour and operating costs than many developed countries.
Good IT infrastructure and supportive government policies in many cities.

answer.en: Skills, cost, time zone and infrastructure.
